chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Baseer prayed Salat with us in a street of Makkah, and he said while he was prostrating, and a she-camel of their cameleer had strayed, 'O Allah! Return to so and so, his camel'.

Muhammad (the narrator) said, 'So I went over to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and informed him. He said: 'And he did so?' I said, 'Yes'. So he remained silent. I said, 'So, should he repeat the Salat?' He said: 'No'.
ai.seo_question: Does making a supplication for a worldly matter during prostration invalidate the prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the permissibility of making specific worldly supplications (du'a) during the prostration (sajdah) of prayer, as confirmed by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) who remained silent, indicating approval. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the core act of worship remains valid even when the supplicant seeks temporal relief, such as the return of a lost camel, without necessitating prayer repetition. This reflects the flexibility in ritual practice where the spiritual state of humility in sajdah accommodates both divine and worldly needs.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘Abu Baseer prayed Salāt with us in a street of Makkah, and he said while he was prostrating, and a she-camel of their cameleer had strayed, ‘O Allahazwj! Return to so and so, his camel’.

Muhammad (the narrator) said, ‘So I went over to Abu Abdullahasws and informed himasws. Heasws said: ‘And he did so?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So heasws remained silent. I said, ‘So, should he repeat the Salāt?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“Abu Basir once on the way to Makkah performed Salah (prayer) with us as the leader and while in Sajdah (prostration) said, ‘O Lord, - a camel of their camel man was lost-, return to so and so his camel.’

Muhammad has said that I then went to visit abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and informed him (about what abu Basir had said in Sajdah (prostration)). He (the Imam) asked, ‘Did he do so? I replied, ‘Yes, he did.’ He (the Imam) remained quiet. I then asked, ‘Must I perform Salah (prayer) again?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘No, (it is not necessary).”’ (Hadith 8 is best explained in the form of fatwa.)
